verses: Where Chun's suburbs lie remote, From the staffs the oxtails float. High the staffs, and each one bright With its silken bandlets white! Four cars drawn by steeds of fire Welcome guest whom. all desire. Admirable, what will he Give to meet such courtesy?

In Chun's suburbs near the town, Fly the falcon banners, blown From the staffs that rise around, All with bands of white silk bound. Five cars drawn by horses strong Wait the guest who comes along. Courteous, worthy,—what shall he Pay for all this courtesy?

Now the walls of Chun we see; Feather'd streamers flutter free From the flagstaffs strong and stout, "Girt by silken bands about. Six cars drawn by steeds of fame Well attest the guest's high name. Sage profound, what can he say That such welcome will repay?
